newsitem.title: New Zealand: Sri Lanka may play youngster in 1st test.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka may play youngster in 1st test.

text.p: GISBORNE, March 5 - New Zealand could come face to face with a player bearing an uncanny resemblance to the silhouette of former Australian fast bowler Bruce Reid when the first cricket test against Sri Lanka starts in Dunedin on Friday.
Nuwan Zoysa, 18, was playing schoolboy cricket just eight months ago, but he has been fast-tracked into the Sri Lankan side as they seek to beef up their fast bowling stocks.

Beef up is not quite the appropriate term though as Zoysa's 1.96 metre frame carries no sign of excess weight. He's almost a waif-like figure, but Sri Lankan coach Bruce Yardley reckons he can handle the physical rigours of international cricket.

Fellow left-armer Reid's international career for Australia was blighted by recurring back and shoulder problems which repeatedly required surgery. He finally retired a year ago after health problems restricted him to just 33 tests since 1985.
Yardley said watching Zoysa bowl reminded him a lot of Reid, whom he considered one of the best bowlers he had seen.
"He has a very similar approach and runup. Nuwan also has a lovely fast arm action which Reid had as well."
He believes Zoysa will prove that he has more strength than the former Western Australian quick bowler.

"Bruce Reid had no muscle strength whatsoever. They tried to build him up but there was nothing to build on. Nuwan is not as skinny as Bruce was and he has more strength than him," said Yardley, a former Western Australian and Australian offspinner.
Zoysa was supposed to make his first appearance for Sri Lanka in their tour match against New Zealand A here this week but rain meant no play was possible over the previous three days.
Yardley is sorely tempted to pitch Zoysa straight into the first test at Carisbrook, and told NZPA that the youngster should not be held back because of his tender years.
"We are looking to the future with him, but I'd like to get him started now because I reckon he's up to it.
"He gets tremendous bounce off the track and is a bit different to anything Sri Lanka have ever had before.
"He has got to be played sometime and I reckon it's a matter of sooner rather than later.
"We'll have to wait and see what the pitch is like in Dunedin, but Nuwan gets a bit of bounce which is handy on any deck."

Zoysa is one of five fast-medium bowlers in the 15-man Sri Lankan tour party. The Sri Lankans believe they need to bolster their pace attack to achieve their goal of becoming the best test nation in the world by the year 2000.

Others among the pace battery are left armer Chaminda Vaas, who has developed splendidly despite still being only 22. His 14 tests to date have already seen Vaas capture 54 wickets at a world-class average of 23.87. He destroyed New Zealand two years ago when he took 16 wickets in two tests.
Another left armer is Sajeewa de Silva, who is a little quicker through the air than Vaas, but who has appeared in the one-day arena only to date.
The experienced Pramodya Wickremasinghe, 25, has played 23 tests without setting the world alight and Ravindra Pushpakumara, at 21, is still feeling his way after a number of overseas tours.
Pushpakumara, who toured here two years ago when Sri Lanka won their maiden test series abroad, is being encouraged to refine his trademark runup.

"Ravindra has usually operated off a runup of 40 paces but he's lately been off balance in his delivery stride. I've worked on him in the past week to reduce it and he's now down to 27 paces. I think we can get it down to 20 and he loses none of his pace," Yardley said.
